version: V.01 passive spring hug, Mirumi proportions (one egg body, two short symmetric shoulder arms, centre groove)
official_FS90MG: datasheets/FS90MG.pdf p.5, edition A/0, 2021-04-30, all ±0.1 mm

servos.head_pan: Feetech FS90 in yaw_collar, software ±42°, hard stop ±47°
servos.head_tilt: Feetech FS90 on neck_turret, axis along x through y=6, z=119; software ±10°, first contact +13.5° (nod down) / -23.5° (look up)

hug.mechanism: Mirumi-style passive hug: each arm turns on a vertical M3 shoulder pin just under the face (knuckle z 70–86); a music-wire torsion spring in the knuckle closes it onto a printed rest stop (30° preload); opened by hand to a 60° printed stop; zero power to hold. Two short symmetric arms whose paws nearly meet in front of the handle

spring.part: music-wire torsion spring, 0.048 in (1.22 mm) wire, 3/8 in (9.5 mm) OD, 90° legs (trim to ~6 mm); catalogue 3HPG6 (LH) / 3HPD1 (RH)

hug.arm_angle_convention: 0 = closed on the rest stop, + = open; rotation about z through each shoulder (x=±44.6, y=−31.2)
hug.groove: R8 channel down the front centre, 1.7° from vertical (for a handle upright), floor 2.5 mm (z 48) to 4 mm (z 80) below the skin, capsule z ≈ 36–94 (up to the torso rim), 2.4 mm liner; paws meet at z ≈ 70 (upper chest)

grip.object: round Ø10.0 upright in the centre groove (1.7° from the body vertical)
round Ø12.5 upright in the centre groove (1.7° from the body vertical)
round Ø15.0 upright in the centre groove (1.7° from the body vertical)
flat strap 25 x 2.5 across the groove mouth, along the groove line

open.note: Ø15 x 50 rod brought in on a straight line perpendicular to its axis (90 mm travel) onto the groove floor, both arms on the open stop; checked against both rigid arms, both pads and torso_front. NOTE: until the thick-arm pass this check iterated over an empty range (np.arange with the wrong step sign) and so always passed; with the old 30 deg stop no straight path exists.

hug.assumption: Spring rate from the catalogue (2.679 lbf·in at 90°), linear; no hinge friction; the two symmetric arms close from either side and their paws press on the front quarters of the handle; pad normal force = spring torque / |(r x n)_z| at the deepest pad contact. TPU pads assumed rigid for the angle (real pads add ~1 mm of squash). Not measured.

arm_min_clearance_mm.note: arm_to_shell 0 = the stop lug resting on its relief face (by design); knuckle to ear is 0.4 mm

proportions.shell_mm: Ø92 x 148 (one egg: R46 at z58, superellipse n=3.4 dome; kept at 148 mm to clear the tilt servo / neck_turret at z ≈ 140)
proportions.with_fur_mm: ≈137 wide (round ball torso R60 + ≈8 mm v3 pile) x ≈125 head ball x ≈162 tall seated (head ball top z 155 + crown pile); v3-bear look, Mirumi clasp

seated_on_bag.note: Mirumi pose: bottom resting on the bag top, both arms round the handle. The bag carries the weight; the springs hold it upright against the handle.

free_hang.note: Hanging free from a vertical handle upright (nothing under it): slip down the handle is resisted only by friction on the pads and the groove; the COM offset from the handle is carried as a moment by the pad / groove couple.

seated_on_bag.note: Mirumi pose: bottom resting on the bag top, both arms round the handle. The bag carries the weight; the springs hold it upright against the handle.

free_hang.note: Hanging free from a vertical handle upright (nothing under it): slip down the handle is resisted only by friction on the pads and the groove; the COM offset from the handle is carried as a moment by the pad / groove couple.

clinging.assumption: Handle Ø12.5 upright on the centre groove floor line (≈2° from the body vertical). μ = 0.5 TPU/fur on a fabric or leather handle (ASSUMED). Pad forces from scripts/sim_v01.py. Not tested.

servo_power.note: Arms are passive and draw nothing. FS90 stall 700 mA at 4.8 V (Feetech). U3V16F5 from a 3.7 V cell gives roughly 1 A continuous at 5 V, so the firmware must not stall both servos at once; the INA219 trip covers it.

runtime.note: XIAO ESP32S3 Sense Wi-Fi active ≈110 mA (Seeed), servos moving ~20 % of the time ≈60 mA average (ASSUMED): ≈2 h; ≈3–4 h with Wi-Fi light-sleep between interactions.
